- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate early spikes; reduce forecast magnitude by 15–30% for first 5–7 days after sentiment spike.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates downside risk; add 10–25% buffer to low-end forecasts, especially for first 3–5 days.
- Model consistently overestimates 30-day horizon tail risk (last 5–7 days) after sentiment shifts; apply 20–40% downward correction to final 5–7 days if sentiment turns negative.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in 30-day forecasts when sentiment is neutral or mixed; apply 5–15% upward adjustment to middle 10–15 days if sentiment is 0.00–0.33.
- Overshoots after sentiment spikes (e.g., 1.00) often occur in 10–15 day horizon; cap forecast at 1.2x historical max for 10–15 day window if sentiment > 0.75.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00/0.33 patterns, model tends to underestimate true volatility; increase forecast variance by 10–20% for 10–20 day horizon.
